target_customer: Banks, fintechs and lenders in Mexico and Latin America that run collections and sales call centers
problem: Collections call centers are costly and hard to scale. Altur runs collections and sales conversations with AI agents over voice, WhatsApp and SMS.
business_model: B2B usage-based AI call center platform (pricing not public)
product_category: Voice AI agents for debt collection

founders.name: Luis Olave
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders spent about 2 years in debt collections in Mexico, first with WhatsApp chatbots, then voice. Education and employers not listed.

founders.name: Pedro Fernández
founders.background_notes: Education and employers not listed in sources opened.

competitors.name: Murphy
competitors.what: AI agents for debt servicing for utilities, telcos, banks and BNPL firms, based in Spain
competitors.funding_then: 15 million dollars combined pre-seed and seed

competitors.name: DROS.ai (Vodex)
competitors.what: Voice agents with compliance guardrails for collection agencies and debt buyers

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents with negotiation, a dialer, multichannel follow up and compliance logging are standard applied AI work using commercial speech and language models, with hard parts in latency and Spanish language phone quality.

defensibility.rationale: Bank integrations and ISO 27001 certification add friction, but underlying models are shared and many voice AI collections vendors exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded collections voice AI vendors existed by mid 2025, but no incumbent was reported to target Mexican banks specifically.

market_need_then: Collections are labor heavy and Altur's customers include large Mexican lenders. YC's launch post says it collected over 6 million dollars with only AI agents after launching in Mexico.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, for example hire your AI call center and Human-less Call Center

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning line but little brand press or community; name origin unknown and a name collision with an unrelated manufacturer of the same name.

pivots.from: WhatsApp chatbots for debt collection in Mexico
pivots.why: YC page says the founders began with WhatsApp chatbots and moved to voice; exact date not stated

outcome_analysis: Altur is active and appears to have early traction with large Mexican financial customers, backed by YC's claim of over 6 million dollars collected by AI agents. The founders spent two years in Mexican collections before moving from chatbots to voice, which fits the timing of voice model improvements. Funding is not credibly sourced and the outcome is open.
notes: Funding figures conflict across aggregators (125K, 500K, 600K, 1.5M seed; Platanus and NuMundo named once) and are all unverified, so no round is recorded. Headquarters is reported as Mexico City by YC and Monterrey or San Francisco elsewhere. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news found.
